label: sprites/fw_spit.spr: a sludge spit that splashes, animated

againstClass.words: flickers: more coherence from frame to frame

R1.reason: It reads as a puffy glowing gas burst with a starburst of sparks at its core (frames 1-4), not as wet sludge spit splashing. There are no heavy globs or droplets thrown outward and falling, and no splash crown. The thin lines in frames 4-6 look more like spark trails than drips. The effect is close to a spit or splash, but a player would more likely call it a small green explosion or gas puff.

R2.reason: It is 64x64, a normal size for a spit or splash sprite. The effect is centred and grows to fill most of the frame by frames 4-5 without reaching the edges (border mean 0, within the explosion class range). Frames 0 and 9 are empty, but that is the class's one-shot opening and ending (first 0, last 0, both in range).

R3.reason: Blended additively it shows a green that fits the brief's grey-green sludge, and it dulls to a darker grey-green as it fades (frames 6-8). There is no neon or sci-fi hue. The hot yellow-white core in frames 1-3 is a little bright for sludge, but it is short and small. No mean-colour measure was given, so this is judged from the sheet.

R4.reason: The measured jitter of 1.62 is outside the explosion class range of 1.04-1.48, which caps this item at 1. The sheet shows why: the blob clusters change arrangement from frame to frame (for example frames 2 to 3 and 5 to 6) instead of moving outward together, so it flickers rather than reading as one splash spreading. The rest of the motion is right: 10 frames, a peak at 0.44, and it starts and ends dark as a one-shot should.

R5.reason: It is a parallel sprite in additive format, which suits a glowing spit effect that the brief leaves unspecified. It has the name the brief implies (sprites/fw_spit.spr), and its 10 frames at 64x64 read back as written.
